issues.title: Missing router import causes undefined variable error in BookerWebWrapper
issues.description: The `useRouter` hook is removed from the imports but the `router` variable is still used in multiple places within the component (lines 193, 228, 233, 239). This will cause a ReferenceError at runtime when any of these code paths are executed, such as when toggling the overlay calendar, navigating for instant meetings, or handling calendar interactions. The router is critical for navigation functionality in the booking flow.

issues.title: Incorrect priority sorting in sortHosts breaks round-robin host assignment
issues.description: The priority comparison logic is inverted when weights are equal in round-robin mode. The code now returns `priorityA - priorityB` instead of `priorityB - priorityA`, which sorts hosts in ascending priority order (lowest priority first) instead of descending (highest priority first). This causes lower-priority hosts to be selected before higher-priority hosts when weights are equal, breaking the intended assignment logic throughout the application wherever host assignment is used.

issues.title: Missing module resolution in dynamic import causes team assignment tab to fail
issues.description: The EventTeamAssignmentTab dynamic import is missing the `.then((mod) => mod)` module resolution that all other tab imports use. This inconsistency will cause the dynamic import to not properly extract the default export, resulting in the team assignment tab failing to render correctly. When users navigate to the team assignment tab for event types, they will encounter a blank screen or rendering error because the component cannot be properly loaded.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26629 - refactor: move WebWrapper files from packages/platform to apps/web/modules

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves the WebWrapper components (EventTypeWebWrapper and its tab wrappers, BookerWebWrapper, ConferencingAppsViewWebWrapper, SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper, AddMembersWithSwitchWebWrapper, DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper) from `packages/platform/atoms` into `apps/web`. Its goal is to let them import sibling web modules instead of reaching across packages through `@calcom/web`. It also moves `sortHosts` into `@calcom/lib/bookings/hostGroupUtils`, adds hook exports to the atoms `package.json`, and removes the `booker` and WebWrapper exports from that file.

The move itself is mostly mechanical and the relative-import rewrites look correct. However, I found a definite runtime break and a silent behavior change. `BookerWebWrapper.tsx` drops the `useRouter` import and its `const router` declaration, but `router` is still used in several places (router.push at lines 193, 228, 232, 238), so every booker page would throw a ReferenceError. The `sortHosts` move also flips the comparator's equal-weight branch from `priorityB - priorityA` to `priorityA - priorityB`, which reverses host ordering in round-robin-weights mode across three callers. The atoms package also still exports `./booker` pointing at a deleted `index.ts`, and nothing in the PR exercises any of this (the only verification step is type-check, which would not catch the bad `sortHosts` order).
structured_output.verdictRationale: The PR should not merge as is. The missing `useRouter` declaration breaks every Booker page at runtime, and it is the kind of error a type-check run would surface, so the author's stated test plan would catch it only if it actually runs. The `sortHosts` comparator flip is a silent ordering regression with no test coverage. The stale `./booker` export in the atoms package breaks the atoms build for anyone who imports it. The remaining items are cleanup.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, the WebWrapper components lived in `packages/platform/atoms` and imported the real web components back through `@calcom/web/modules/...`, so the atoms package depended on the web app. The web pages under `apps/web/app` and `apps/web/modules` consumed those wrappers through `@calcom/atoms/...` subpath exports. The PR relocates each wrapper into the matching `apps/web/modules/<feature>/components` directory so it can use sibling relative imports. The web app then depends on the atoms package only for the leaf platform pieces it still needs: the event-type hooks, `SelectedCalendarsSettings`, and `DestinationCalendar`.

The PR also moves `sortHosts` out of a web component file and into a shared `packages/lib` utility, so the atoms hook `useEventTypeForm` no longer imports from `apps/web`. The atoms `package.json` exports are updated to match: the WebWrapper subpaths are removed and the hook and SelectedCalendarsSettings subpaths are added. The `./booker` export is left pointing at a file that was deleted.
steps: Start at the entry points: Next.js pages under `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)` and the view modules under `apps/web/modules/{team,users,d,org}` now import the Booker, EventType, and calendar wrappers from `@calcom/web/modules/...` paths or from the relocated `apps/web/modules/*/components` files.

Within `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx`, the dynamic tab imports now resolve to sibling `./tabs/*` wrappers. Those wrappers in turn import their tab components with relative paths. Only the form hooks still come from `@calcom/atoms/event-types/hooks/*`.

`BookerWebWrapper.tsx` moves to `apps/web/modules/bookings/components` and imports `./Booker` relatively. This is the file where the PR removes `useRouter` and its `router` binding, which the rest of the component still depends on.

`sortHosts` moves to `packages/lib/bookings/hostGroupUtils.ts`. Its three consumers are `EventTeamAssignmentTab`, `HostEditDialogs`, and the atoms hook `useEventTypeForm`, which now imports it from `@calcom/lib`.

`DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper` moves into `apps/web/components/apps` but reaches back into `packages/platform/atoms` through deep relative paths, which the PR description was trying to avoid. The atoms `package.json` exports map is also updated to drop removed subpaths and add the new hook subpaths, while the `./booker` entry is left dangling.

findings.title: BookerWebWrapper uses `router` after its declaration was removed
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookerWebWrapper.tsx`, the PR removed `useRouter` from the `next/navigation` import and removed `const router = useRouter();` from `BookerWebWrapperComponent`. But `router.push` is still used at about lines 193, 228, 232, and 238, and `[router]` is in a dependency array at line 195. Restore the `useRouter` import on the existing `next/navigation` import line, and restore the `const router = useRouter();` declaration next to `pathname` and `searchParams` in `BookerWebWrapperComponent`, matching the original file in `packages/platform/atoms/booker/BookerWebWrapper.tsx`. Keep the other unused-import removals (`useRef`, the `BookerComponent` import path) as they are. Confirm with `tsc --noEmit` or the type-check step that no references to `router` remain undefined.

findings.title: sortHosts comparator order is inverted for equal weights
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/lib/bookings/hostGroupUtils.ts`, the `sortHosts` function was moved from `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/HostEditDialogs.tsx` but its equal-weight branch was changed. In the RR-weights branch (around line 52-54), the original returned `priorityB - priorityA`, and the moved version returns `priorityA - priorityB`, which reverses host order for hosts with equal weight. Restore the original comparator exactly so the move is behavior-preserving. Callers are `EventTeamAssignmentTab.tsx` (lines 324 and 332), `HostEditDialogs.tsx` (lines 82 and 178), and `packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts` line 103. After the fix, add a unit test in `packages/lib/bookings` covering equal weights in RR mode, to lock in the expected order.

findings.title: Atoms package still exports a deleted `./booker` entry point
findings.body:
The PR deletes `packages/platform/atoms/booker/index.ts`, but the atoms `package.json` still maps `"./booker"` to `./booker/index.ts`. Anything that resolves `@calcom/atoms/booker` now fails at module resolution. In the same directory, `booker/export.ts` still does `export { BookerWebWrapper as Booker } from "./BookerWebWrapper";`, but `BookerWebWrapper.tsx` was moved out. That breaks the atoms dist build, which uses `export.ts`.

I checked the web app and found no remaining `@calcom/atoms/booker` imports, so the web build is not affected by this specific entry. The PR's own checklist still asks to confirm that no external consumer depends on the removed `@calcom/atoms/booker` export, and the answer is not verified in this diff.

::diff{file="packages/platform/atoms/package.json" lines="54-72"}

The fix is to remove the `"./booker"` export and also remove or rewrite `packages/platform/atoms/booker/export.ts`, which still points at `./BookerWebWrapper`. If the platform Booker entry is still needed, point it at `BookerPlatformWrapper` instead.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/platform/atoms/package.json`, the `"./booker"` export (line 58) still maps to `./booker/index.ts`, which was deleted in this PR. Remove the entry. Also, `packages/platform/atoms/booker/export.ts` still re-exports `BookerWebWrapper` from `./BookerWebWrapper`, which was moved to `apps/web/modules/bookings/components`. Either delete `booker/export.ts` if the atoms dist no longer needs a Booker entry, or change it to export the platform Booker (`BookerPlatformWrapper`) that remains in that folder. Run the atoms package build to confirm it still succeeds, and grep for any remaining `@calcom/atoms/booker` import.

findings.title: Deep relative cross-package imports in DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper
findings.body:
The moved `DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper` now imports from `../../../../packages/platform/atoms/...`. That's the same cross-package reach the PR was meant to remove, and it bypasses the `@calcom/atoms` export map the rest of the codebase uses. The relative path also depends on the file's depth inside `apps/web/components/apps`. A future move will silently break it.

The PR description explicitly lists the `@calcom/atoms` package alias as the preferred path (it used it in `EventTypeWebWrapper`). `DestinationCalendarSettings` can be imported as `@calcom/atoms/destination-calendar/DestinationCalendar`, which keeps this file consistent with `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`. Either add that subpath export or confirm an existing one covers it.

::diff{file="apps/web/components/apps/DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper.tsx" lines="1-8"}

Note: the `AtomsWrapper` import has the same problem and may need an export of its own.
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/web/components/apps/DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper.tsx`, the two imports on lines 3-4 use deep relative paths (`../../../../packages/platform/atoms/...`) to reach into the atoms package. Replace them with `@calcom/atoms/...` package-alias imports, following the pattern used by `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` and `EventAdvancedTab`. Add the needed subpath exports (`./destination-calendar/DestinationCalendar` and an `AtomsWrapper` path) to `packages/platform/atoms/package.json` if they are not already exported. Verify the component still renders on the calendar settings page.

findings.title: No tests cover the moved sortHosts logic or the relocated wrappers
findings.fixPrompt: Add a unit test file next to `packages/lib/bookings/hostGroupUtils.ts` (for example `hostGroupUtils.test.ts`) that covers `sortHosts`. Cover three cases: RR weights disabled, which sorts by priority descending; RR weights enabled with different weights, which sorts by weight descending; and RR weights enabled with equal weights, which should sort by priority descending to match the original behavior. Assert the sorted order of an array, not just that the function returns a number. Use the existing test conventions in the `packages/lib` tests.

findings.title: tabMap JSX reindented to a non-project style
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx`, the `setup` and `availability` entries of `tabMap` (around lines 234-251) were reindented to 8-space and 4-space JSX attributes. Revert them to the same indentation used by the `team` entry below them so the file matches the project's Prettier/Biome formatting. Run the project's formatter on this file to confirm no diff remains.

findings.title: Two wrapper files lost their trailing newline
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/limits/EventLimitsTabWebWrapper.tsx` (line 8) and `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/recurring/EventRecurringWebWrapper.tsx` (line 8), the file ends without a trailing newline after `export default ...;`. Add a newline at the end of each file so they match the original rename.

findings.title: Web app now imports hooks from the atoms package, the opposite of the goal
findings.fixPrompt: Track as a follow-up: `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx` imports `useEventTypeForm`, `useHandleRouteChange`, and `useTabsNavigations` from `@calcom/atoms/event-types/hooks/*` (lines 29-31). Once the hooks can move into `apps/web/modules/event-types`, relocate them and update the imports to sibling paths. No change is needed in this PR, but the atoms `package.json` exports for those hooks should be removed in that later change.

findings.title: Wrappers relocated cleanly, removing reverse dependency on @calcom/web
findings.body:
Most moved files now use sibling relative imports (for example `./EventAdvancedTab`, `./AddMembersWithSwitch`, `./tabs/*/EventTeamAssignmentTab`, and `./Booker`). That removes the platform atoms package's reverse dependency on `@calcom/web/modules/...`, which was the root problem. The dynamic-import rewrite in `EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx` (for example `import("./tabs/instant/EventInstantTab")`) matches the new folder structure. `ConferencingAppsViewWebWrapper` now imports `./AppList` and `./DisconnectIntegrationModal`, which are siblings in the same folder, and `loading.tsx` still gets `SkeletonLoader` from the moved file.

::file{file="apps/web/modules/apps/components/ConferencingAppsViewWebWrapper.tsx"}
